summary: Friday demand pass for How Tech Works: subsea internet cables are a proven Short lane (5.78M, 3.73M and 2.93M views, two of them breakouts at 22-28x their channel), so I added two cable topics: TAT-8, the first cable to carry light across an ocean, and inside the hose-wide seabed cable. The 'how AI works' Shorts are crowded and none reach 1M, so there is no AI Short format.
why: The internet is a core lane in profile.md and the Shorts feed had no internet topic. The references are real breakouts (The Rundown AI 5.78M on 203K, Cernab 3.73M on 168K), and the new topics score 9.31 and 9.47, the top of the feed. 22 history-year facts lacked a fixed flag and would have gone stale.

findings.title: Subsea-cable Shorts are a breakout lane
findings.detail: TAT-8 Short 5.78M on 203K subscribers (28.5x); '$8 Billion Cable' 3.73M on 168K (22.2x); anchors-and-sharks Short 2.93M.

findings.title: AI explainer Shorts are crowded
findings.detail: Most 'how AI / ChatGPT works' Shorts from the last 3 months have under 30K views; the best is 197K (32x). None reaches 1M, so there's no new format.

findings.title: First Short breakout for zoom_inside
findings.detail: Cernab's cable Short (3.73M, 22.2x) is now zoom_inside's top example, and it weakens the 'no breakout reference' premise of tech-zoom-short-demand.

findings.title: Claude Code still 2.1.332
